attacks.claim: S4's premise 'still zero store-internal uses' for MidiController is false: store.svelte.ts contains 11 `this.midi.*` uses beyond the forwarders — openInput at :979, release at :1016, applyNoteLearn at :1065 and :1467, applyCcLearn at :1078, startLearn at :1915, cancelLearn at :1919 — so the step's stated risk basis is wrong even though the mechanic happens to survive (the field name `midi` is unchanged, so internal uses compile untouched).
attacks.evidence: grep -n 'this\.midi\.' apps/web/src/lib/trigger-lab/store.svelte.ts returns 11 hits: lines 815,821,826,830 (forwarder bodies) plus 979,1016,1065,1078,1467,1915,1919 (real internal uses in the MIDI forwarding / lifecycle paths).
attacks.repair: Correct S4's text: the field keeps its name so the ~7 non-forwarder internal uses (openInput/release/applyNoteLearn/applyCcLearn/startLearn/cancelLearn) are unaffected by publishing it; the implementer must NOT retarget them and must not treat 'zero internal uses' as a checkable precondition, because it fails.

attacks.claim: The S8/S12 diff-shape gate is weaker than the plan claims: the rg -v whitelist passes ANY +/- line containing a renamed-accessor substring, so a changed expected value on a line that also contains `store.library.` (e.g. `expect(store.library.songs.length).toBe(3)` -> `toBe(2)`) slips through, and equal per-file numstat is preserved by any 1-for-1 line edit — the gate cannot actually detect a weakened assertion on a retargeted line.
attacks.evidence: S8 verification: "git diff -U0 | rg '^[+-]' | rg -v 'store\\.arrangement\\.|\\.activeSectionId|...'" — the -v filter excludes whole lines by substring, and every retargeted assertion line necessarily contains the new accessor substring, so edits to the rest of that line are invisible to the gate.
attacks.repair: Replace the rg gate with a rename-normalised diff: `git show <base>:file | sed 's/store\.activeSectionId/store.arrangement.activeSectionId/g; ...' | diff - file` must be empty per file — a mechanical proof that the ONLY change is the accessor path, which is what the step already claims.

attacks.claim: divergent-change-0002 is the initiative's critical finding and this plan answers it with a member-count/LOC ratchet test plus a header comment (S1/S22) while explicitly leaving node/graph authoring, undo, clipboard, WS link, persistence, transport, backups and OSC status converging on a ~3,250-line store.svelte.ts — so the churn axes measured by the finding (Patch Graph v2, undo semantics, splice-on-drop, Mix rows, Backups, OSC panel) still land in one file.
attacks.evidence: Finding divergent-change-0002 (severity critical) claims cross-axis convergence on store.svelte.ts; opus S22 intent concedes 'which still converge on store.svelte.ts (node/graph authoring, undo, clipboard/paste, WS link, persistence, transport, backups, OSC/tunnel status)'.
attacks.plan_response: The plan defends this scoping explicitly and escalates rather than guesses: summary ('Deliberately NOT in scope: a third grand facade... the authoring-document cluster is entangled with undo snapshots, the sim and persistence in a way no mechanical move survives'), known_gaps item (4) ('divergent-change-0002's actual claim... is a claim about FUTURE commits and is unprovable by any run today. The ratchet in S1/S22 is an honest substitute'), and open_questions[2] puts the stop-vs-follow-on decision to Trent with blocks_execution false. Given the settled fact that R20-R24-style leaf extraction is the failure mode being repaired, refusing a third mechanical facade is a defensible answer the plan argues, not an omission.

attacks.claim: S1's surface instrument assumes `new TriggerLab()` is constructible in the node/vitest env and that Svelte 5 compiles class $state/$derived fields to prototype accessors so the prototype walk plus Object.keys captures all 397 members; if either assumption fails the ratchet undercounts silently and every later 'exact EXPECTED_MEMBERS diff' verification is theatre.
attacks.evidence: S1 intent relies on Object.getOwnPropertyNames(Object.getPrototypeOf(store)) ∪ Object.keys(store); Svelte compiler output shape is an implementation detail of svelte 5.x and could route some fields through symbols or instance-defined accessors.
attacks.plan_response: S1's verification includes a bite-proof ('temporarily add `get __probe()`... confirm the test FAILS naming __probe') and pins the count to the independently measured 397 at HEAD, so a silent undercount is caught at authoring time; store.*.test.ts suites already construct the store under this test env (S16 intent cites 'store.*.test.ts already does exactly that'), so constructibility is demonstrated, not assumed.

attacks.evidence: Verified at HEAD: store.svelte.ts:577 `get shows(): { id: string; name: string }[]` and :925 `get sections(): Section[]`; repo-wide `.sections` refs = 177 and `.shows` refs = 44, matching the plan's 176/40 counts.

The names are measured, not asserted.

attacks.claim: S10 lands the AuthoringStore extraction — self-described as ~3000 LOC across '~100+ consumer files' — as ONE commit with no intermediate resting state; if anything is discovered late (a template-only consumer, a host-callback cycle with undo/sim/persistence) the only move is wholesale revert, and the plan's own open_questions[0] doubts the step belongs in this initiative at all. A step the plan itself proposes deferring is not a plan, it is a placeholder.

attacks.claim: S4/S5 publish the controllers under the NAMES of the deleted array-typed forwarders — `get sections(): SectionsController` replaces `get sections(): Section[]` (177 `.sections` refs repo-wide, 89 in trigger-lab tests) and `get shows(): ShowsController` replaces `get shows(): {id,name}[]` (44 refs) — so every existing array read becomes a type error whose fix is the double-hop `store.sections.sections` (SectionsController's own derived is named `sections`, verified at sections-controller.svelte.ts:79). The claimed 'green unmodified except mechanical store.sections.* repoints' hides a type-changing rewrite of ~220 call sites plus a permanent x.sections.sections readability trap, and open_questions[4] only licenses renaming on collision 'with an existing TriggerLab member' — which, post-deletion, no longer exists, so the trap is kept by instruction.
attacks.evidence: Verified at HEAD: store.svelte.ts:577 and :925 (the colliding getters); sections-controller.svelte.ts:79 `sections = $derived.by((): Section[] =>`; repo-wide grep counts `.sections` = 177, `.shows` = 44. The opus variant independently measured the same collision and concluded a different name or a ~500-site rename pass is required.
attacks.repair: Name the published seams so member access reads once (e.g. `arrangement`/`library` per the opus measurement, or Trent's naming answer), OR explicitly plan the two-hop shape with the full 220-site retarget counted in scope and LOC — the current text does neither.

attacks.claim: S9 treats `this.link === 'open'` as save success ('saved() only when the local writes returned true OR the server sync path actually ran (this.link === 'open')') — but the WS send is fire-and-forget with no ack, so with quota exceeded and the link open the indicator still claims Saved on unproven delivery; the finding's realistic trigger (large library + Safari private mode) is precisely a case where the local write fails while the link may be open.
attacks.evidence: resilience-hole-0007 evidence notes syncShowToServer only gates on link state; opus open_questions[1] establishes the same fact ('client.send is fire-and-forget with no ack, so the web cannot know delivery'). fable S9 intent text quotes the OR-gate.
attacks.repair: Gate saved() on local-write success only (conservative default), and record the link-open question as the existing open question for Trent — or name the OR-gate as a deliberate product choice with its false-'Saved' window stated.
